items.title: Exploring The Lived Experiences Of Depression Among Youths And Their Guardians In Sub-Saharan Africa: a Systematic Review and Meta-Aggregation.
items.authors: Makiyi P, Malata W, Udedi M, Kumwenda M, Muula A, January J.
items.journal: Malawi medical journal : the journal of Medical Association of Malawi

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The cultural context influences how mental disorders like depression, are perceived and experienced. Most studies on lived experiences of depression by youths have been done in high-income countries. This has made it difficult for researchers to infer the findings in the context of SSA due to differences in cultures and socio-demographic characteristics. This systematic review thus, seeks to understand how depression is experienced by youths and their guardians in SSA.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This systematic review was done to address two key objectives: to explore and synthesize qualitative studies on the lived experience of depression among youths and their guardians and to identify common themes, and the impact of socio-cultural and contextual factors on the lived experience of depression among youths and their guardians in SSA.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.text: Two research assistants independently searched and selected articles from databases such as PubMed, using a set search strategy. Thereafter, two reviewers reviewed and extracted data from the selected articles, analysed it using meta-aggregation techniques. The identified papers underwent an independent quality assessment using the Critical Appraisal Skills Program checklist by the two independent researchers. Through this quality assessment, the risk of bias in the papers was also assessed. We have used the Preferred Reporting Items of Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines in reporting this review.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Our search resulted into 14 unique studies spanning 8 countries in SSA, representing a total of 610 young people (10 to 24 years; 72% females) with lived experience of depression, 297 caregivers and 70 healthcare workers. Findings on the lived experience of youths were aggregated into eleven categories which were further grouped into three main synthesised findings of making sense of depression, mental health systems and services and contextual issues as key issues encompassing their lived experience. Regarding the experience of guardians, three key themes were identified: challenges faced by the guardians, their perception of youth depression and their experience in navigating through the healthcare system.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The sociocultural context in SSA determines how the youth experience depression and that symptoms of depression as experiences by youths in SSA may not always match diagnostic criteria developed from the west. The experiences of the guardians have an impact on the young people's experiences of depression.

items.title: Psychometric Validation of the German International Depression Questionnaire and the International Anxiety Questionnaire.
items.authors: Bachem R, Bircher C, Eberle DJ, Levin Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The International Depression Questionnaire (IDQ) and the International Anxiety Questionnaire (IAQ) are brief, ICD-11-aligned self-report instruments designed to assess depressive episodes and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). While the initial validation study of the original English versions supported unidimensional structures, further cross-cultural validation is warranted. This study examined the psychometric properties of the German versions of the IDQ and IAQ among German-speaking adults.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 710 participants completed an online survey including the IDQ, IAQ, and additional measures assessing depressive symptoms, anxiety, posttraumatic stress, and adjustment difficulties. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses assessed factorial validity. Internal consistency was evaluated using Cronbach's alpha. Convergent and discriminant validity were examined via partial correlations controlling for age and gender.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Analyses supported a three-factor structure for the IDQ (essential, cognitive-affective, and vegetative symptoms) and a unidimensional structure for the IAQ, as two-factor solutions yielded very highly correlated factors. Both scales demonstrated good model fit and excellent internal consistency ( α  = 0.90 for each scale). The IDQ showed the strongest correlations with depressive symptoms and negative automatic thoughts, while the IAQ correlated most strongly with measures of generalized anxiety. Lower correlations with posttraumatic stress and adjustment problems supported discriminant validity.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The results provide initial evidence that the German versions of the IDQ and IAQ are reliable and valid tools for assessing ICD-11 depression and generalized anxiety. The multidimensional structure of the IDQ supports theoretical distinctions between depressive symptom domains, whereas the IAQ appears best represented by a single generalized anxiety factor. Further replication and validation against external clinical criteria are needed to establish the clinical relevance of these factor structures.

items.title: Healthcare trajectories after an initial diagnosis for mood/anxiety disorders via telehealth versus in-person visit among pregnant women without pre-existing mood/anxiety disorders: Latent growth analyses of electronic medical records.
items.authors: Acharya M, Bogulski CA, Ali MM.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: With telehealth commonly used for mental health diagnosis and management during pregnancy, it is unknown how it affects utilization trajectories.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using a national database of electronic medical records (Epic Cosmos), January 2018-November 2025, among pregnant women without pre-existing anxiety, depression, or bipolar disorders. The initial in-person outpatient or telehealth visit/date during pregnancy with a diagnosis of anxiety/depression/bipolar was considered index visit/date. The sample was followed from the index date for 360 days. Four outcomes with anxiety/depression/bipolar diagnoses were studied for each 30-day follow-up interval: 1) emergency department (ED) visits, 2) hospitalizations, 3) in-person outpatient/office visits, and 4) telehealth visits. Multigroup latent growth models were estimated. Average marginal effects (AME) were reported.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The final sample had 121,818 in-person outpatient and 7,763 telehealth initiators. The average ages were 28.9 years (in-person) and 30.2 years (telehealth); 84% (in-person) and 87% (telehealth) were urban residents. The AMEs of telehealth use for ED visits and hospitalizations were (in percentage points), respectively, -0.128 (-0.216; -0.040) and -0.222 (-0.432; -0.012). Telehealth initiators were less likely to have in-person outpatient visits (AME: -3.607 (-4.028; -3.185)) and more likely to have telehealth visits (AME: 2.741 (2.380; 3.102)).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The initial diagnosis of anxiety, depression, or bipolar conditions via telehealth was associated with similar rates of ED visits and hospitalizations, lower rates of outpatient visits, and higher rates of subsequent telehealth visits.

items.title: Trends in the Prevalence and Incidence of Dissociative Disorders in the United States: A Nationwide Real-World Analysis.
items.authors: Feghali C, Richardson S, Conte B, Hull A, Zheng W.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Dissociative disorders (DD) are associated with substantial functional impairment and psychiatric burden. Epidemiologic evidence of DD, in terms of trends in prevalence, incidence, demographic patterns, psychiatric comorbidities, and medication utilization in the United States remains poorly understood.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, this retrospective study identified 60,362 patients aged ≥5 years with a diagnosis of DD between 2016 and 2025. Annual prevalence and incidence were calculated from a base population of 103,712,997 patients from the platform. Temporal trends were evaluated using joinpoint regression analysis, stratified by sex, race, and age group. Psychiatric comorbidities and psychotropic medication use were assessed during the 1-year and 5-year periods after DD diagnosis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among 60,362 patients with DD (mean age, 50 years; 69.8% female), annual prevalence increased from 57 to 120 per 100,000 between 2016 and 2025. Incidence showed modest increase (11 to 16 per 100,000). While prevalence increased across both sexes, all racial groups, and all age groups, the largest increases were observed among females, individuals aged 15 to 44 years. Other anxiety disorders (37.81%), depressive episode (28.51%), substance use disorders (21.47%), and posttraumatic stress disorder (16.02%) were the most common psychiatric comorbidities within 1 year of DD diagnosis and increased further during follow-up. Antidepressants, sedative-hypnotics, anticonvulsants, and antipsychotics were frequently prescribed and showed increasing use over time.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The prevalence of DD increased substantially in the United States from 2016 to 2025, whereas incidence showed modest changes. DD were associated with a high burden of psychiatric comorbidities and extensive psychotropic medication use, underscoring their clinical complexity and unmet mental health needs. These findings highlight the growing public health relevance of DD and the need for improved recognition and early intervention.

items.title: Prevalence and Correlates of Depression in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis at a Tertiary Care Center in Kerala.
items.authors: Abdul Rezak Parayil A, Punnoose V, Alex S.

sections.text: Introduction Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a disabling illness with significant physical, psychological and social consequences. Patients undergoing hemodialysis are at increased risk of developing depressive disorders. Biochemical derangements associated with kidney disease, compounded by the psychological burden of physical and social disability, are established contributory factors. Data on the prevalence and correlates of depression in CKD patients in Kerala remain scarce. Identification of depression in early stages is important in CKD patients as it is a significant predictor of disease progression, hemodialysis initiation, hospitalization, and death. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of depression in CKD patients on maintenance hemodialysis and to identify any sociodemographic, clinical, or biochemical correlates. Materials and methods A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted in the Department of Nephrology, Government T.D. Medical College, Alappuzha, Kerala, over a period of one year. A total of 120 participants were enrolled in the study using consecutive sampling. Sociodemographic, clinical, and biochemical data were collected using a specially designed proforma. Depression was clinically diagnosed by a psychiatrist using ICD-10 Diagnostic Criteria for Research (ICD-10-DCR). The severity of the depressive episode was assessed using the Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II). Data were analyzed using appropriate statistical tests. Multiple linear and binary logistic regression analyses were performed to identify the variables independently associated with the diagnosis of depression and depressive symptom severity. Results The prevalence of depression was 42.5% (51 of 120 patients; 95% CI 34.0-51.4%). Among depressed participants, severity was mild in 18 (35.3%), moderate in 26 (51.0%), and severe in 7 (13.7%). The mean BDI-II score for the whole sample was 17.25 ± 6.59. In univariate analysis, depression was significantly associated with socioeconomic status, low body mass index, shorter duration of dialysis, erythropoietin therapy, hyponatremia, hypocalcemia, lower hemoglobin, lower serum albumin, and higher high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). In multiple linear regression, lower hemoglobin (β = -0.267, p = 0.002) and lower serum sodium (β = -0.236, p = 0.006) remained independently associated with a higher BDI-II score, with the model accounting for 30.8% of the variance (adjusted R² = 0.271, F = 8.367, p < 0.001). In binary logistic regression, hemoglobin was the only variable independently associated with depression status, with each 1 g/dL lower hemoglobin corresponding to 8.20-fold higher odds of depression (95% CI 2.56-26.32, p < 0.001); hyponatremia fell just short of conventional significance (adjusted OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.00-6.54, p = 0.051). Conclusion The high prevalence of depression among CKD patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis suggests that clinicians should actively screen for depressive symptoms in these patients, especially those with the identified biochemical risk factors, to enable early identification and improve quality of life.

items.title: Relationship between digital media use, social connections, and depression in middle-aged and older adults.
items.authors: Chen B, Cao Y, Tang Y, Huang G, Zhong Y, Jiang S, Zhao F, Wang D.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Depression is a prevalent mental health issue among middle-aged and older adults. This study aimed to explore the relationships between digital media use, social connections (structural, functional, and quality components), and depression in this population, and to examine the mediating effect of social connections.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: From April to September 2025, a multi-stage stratified random sampling method was employed to select 1624 middle-aged and older adults from Zhejiang Province, China. Information on digital media use, social connections, and depressive symptoms was collected. Univariate analysis, binary logistic regression were performed, followed by exploratory mediation analysis using the PROCESS macro for SPSS. Clustered CR2 was used as a sensitivity analysis for small-sample inference.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The prevalence of depressive symptoms was 15.58%. Marital status, personal monthly income, frequency of contact with children, living status, self-rated health, and life stress were significantly associated with depressive symptoms ( p <0.05). Greater usability competence (OR=0.884, 95%CI=0.818-0.956, p =0.008) and larger social network size (OR=0.692, 95%CI= 0.539-0.889, p =0.013) were associated with lower odds of depression, while higher loneliness (OR=1.592, 95%CI=1.430-1.771, p <0.001) was associated with higher odds. Exploratory analyses identified statistically significant indirect associations between specific digital media use dimensions (social and entertainment, usability competence and usability competence) and depression through social connection components (social network size, loneliness, social Satisfaction), consistent with partial mediation and suppression patterns.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: These findings indicate that digital media use and social connection components are associated with depression risk in the study sample. Usability competence, social network size, and loneliness showed the most robust associations. The observed associations suggest the potential research value of both online digital engagement and offline social connection factors in mental health. Future longitudinal or intervention studies are needed to further examine the temporal and dynamic relationships between these factors and depression.

items.title: Caregiver burden, family resilience, and depressive and anxiety symptoms in parents of depressed adolescents: a cross-sectional mediation study.
items.authors: Meng M, Shen H, Zhang J, Han Y, Fang X, Wen Y, Cheng C, Yuan Y, Wang C, Lv Q, Yi Z.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Parents of adolescents with depression experience substantial caregiving burden, contributing to an increased risk of psychological distress. While individual resilience has been associated with this relationship, the role of family-level resilience remains underexplored. This study explored whether family resilience statistically accounted for the association between caregiver burden and psychological distress, and whether social support moderated this pathway.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 178 parents of adolescents diagnosed with depression. Participants completed measures of caregiver burden (Zarit Burden Interview, ZBI), family resilience (Family Resilience Assessment Scale, FRAS), social support (Social Support Rating Scale, SSRS), depressive symptoms (Patient Health Questionnaire-9, PHQ-9), and anxiety symptoms (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7, GAD-7). A moderated mediation model (PROCESS Model 7) was tested as the primary analysis, with 5,000 bootstrap resamples, adjusting for child age, child sex, illness duration, caregiver age, caregiver sex, caregiver education and economic status. All continuous predictors were standardized. Sensitivity analyses were re-run on the primary model excluding outliers and using 10,000 bootstrap resamples.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The index of moderated mediation was not significant for depressive symptoms (β = -0.029, 95% CI [-0.086, 0.029], p = 0.262) or anxiety symptoms (β = -0.023, 95% CI [-0.073, 0.021], p = 0.266), indicating that social support did not moderate the indirect pathway. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of these findings.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Family resilience partially accounted for the association between caregiver burden and psychological distress in parents of adolescents with MDD. Social support did not moderate this pathway but was independently associated with higher family resilience. Interventions targeting family resilience may be promising, with social support as a supplementary resource. Longitudinal studies are needed to establish causality and to clarify which aspects of social support are most valued by these caregivers.

items.title: Symptom interactions of insomnia, anxiety, and depression in early pregnancy: a network analysis perspective.
items.authors: Li Y, Jiao L, Cui J, Cui J, Huo L, Zhang Y, Niu L, Niu Y, Bai X, Zhang D.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Pregnancy is a unique phase involving significant physical, social, and psychological changes, increasing vulnerability to anxiety, depression, and insomnia. These conditions are interrelated and often overlap, yet their symptom-symptom relationships during early pregnancy remain underexplored.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 1,830 women in early pregnancy (≤12 weeks) who attended the Children's Hospital of Shanxi Province /Shanxi Maternal and Child Health Hospital, China, between 2021 and 2024 were included. Anxiety and depression were assessed with the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and insomnia with the Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS). Regularized partial correlation networks (EBICglasso applied to polychoric correlations) were estimated to examine the connections among symptoms of anxiety, depression, and insomnia; node centrality and bridge symptoms connecting the three symptom clusters were examined, and the accuracy and stability of the estimates were assessed with bootstrapping.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: In total, 148 women (8.09%) screened positive for depression, 115 (6.28%) for anxiety, and 316 (17.27%) for insomnia. In the symptom network, the symptoms with the highest point estimates of strength centrality were 'I feel as if I am slowed down' (depression), a reduced sense of well-being during the day (insomnia), and 'I feel cheerful' (depression, reverse-scored); these symptoms did not differ reliably from one another or from several other symptoms in bootstrapped difference tests. The same symptoms, together with 'worrying thoughts go through my mind' (anxiety) and 'I can sit at ease and feel relaxed' (anxiety, reverse-scored), showed the highest bridge strength, and this set of five bridge symptoms was identical across all four correlation and estimation methods examined. Bridge expected influence, which retains the direction of the associations, identified the slowed-down item and the worry item as the strongest bridge symptoms.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Anxiety, depression, and insomnia are common, interconnected concerns in early pregnancy. Targeting the core and bridge symptoms identified here may enhance intervention effectiveness; however, causal inferences require longitudinal or experimental validation.

items.title: A systematic review of the existing parent-led interventions to promote the psychosocial development of neurodivergent children.
items.authors: Burnley A, Burke C, Dack C, Wren Y, St Clair MC.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: This systematic review takes a transdiagnostic approach to understanding the active components commonly used across evidence-based interventions, to inform the development of a novel psychosocial intervention for children with Developmental Language Disorder (DLD).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Searches were conducted in December 2020, August 2022 and July 2026 of 11 databases, including: PsycINFO, PsycEXTRA, Embase, PubMed, Cochrane CENTRAL and MEDLINE. Inclusion criteria was: trials must have compared interventions to a control group, or have an 8-week follow-up, include parent-led components and measures of child psychosocial outcomes, must be published in English after 2000, with participants aged 2-13 years old, who met diagnostic criteria for seven categories of neurodivergence (that share psychosocial difficulties to children with DLD). Synthesis was conducted by coding intervention content using a taxonomy and calculating effect sizes using baseline and follow-up data on psychosocial outcomes. Quality appraisal was assessed using the National Institute of Health's quality assessment measures.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 11,583 studies were selected for abstract screening; 52 studies met the pre-specified inclusion criteria after full-text screening. All interventions analysed were designed for autistic children ( n  = 26) and/or attention deficit hyperactive disorder (ADHD; n  = 23). Across studies, 870 children with ADHD and 832 autistic children received interventions; 730 children with ADHD and 701 autistic children received a control. Four intervention components were most used across effective interventions: parent-child interaction training, parenting behaviours, and emotion management for both parent and child. An association between parent wellbeing and improved child psychosocial outcomes is suggested, however limited by the lack of data. Therapeutic and researcher contact appears to impact intervention engagement. Accessibility is discussed.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Evidence-based psychosocial interventions are required for neurodivergent children other than children with autism and ADHD. Psychosocial interventions for children with DLD should consider addressing parent-child communication, wellbeing of both parent and child, and involve therapeutic support.

items.title: Accounting for psychiatric conditions when defining multimorbidity among ethno-racial groups of students in higher education.
items.authors: Oh H, Hajek A, Thomas Tobin CS, Smith L, Jacob L.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Multimorbidity is often overlooked in young people. More research is needed to determine how it should be defined in this population and how including psychiatric conditions affects overall and race/ethnicity-specific prevalence estimates.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Using data from the Healthy Minds Study (N = 96,050; September 2020-June 2021)-a weighted, nonprobability sample of students aged 18-29 years-we estimated the prevalence of multimorbidity based on 13 physical and 10 psychiatric conditions. We also used multivariable logistic regression to examine associations between race/ethnicity and physical, psychiatric, mixed, and any multimorbidity.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The prevalence of multimorbidity was 5.3% for physical, 26.5% for psychiatric, 14.2% for mixed, and 32.2% for any multimorbidity. By unweighted co-occurrence count, the most common pair-wise co-occurences were asthma and other chronic disease for physical conditions, anxiety and depression for psychiatric conditions, and anxiety and asthma for mixed conditions. Including psychiatric conditions substantially increased the prevalence of any multimorbidity, with the largest absolute increase among American Indian/Alaska Native students and White students.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This study explored the value of integrating physical and psychiatric conditions into a working definition of multimorbidity in a large sample of young adult students in higher education in the United States. The findings show how the operational definition of multimorbidity can differentially affect prevalence estimates across racial/ethnic groups.

items.title: Prevalence and Symptom Network of Co-Occurring Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms and Their Associations with Quality of Life Among Chinese Empty-Nest Older Adults.
items.authors: Wang L, Wang P, Li Y, Liu M, Zhao M, Yu J, Cao J, Sun C.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The growing number of empty-nest older adults in China has become a critical public health concern. Living apart from adult children may reduce opportunities for daily family interaction and emotional support and increase feelings of loneliness, potentially increasing vulnerability to anxiety and depressive symptoms. The aim of this study was to investigate the prevalence and network structure of co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms, and explored their association with quality of life (QoL) among Chinese empty-nest older adults.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We included 5110 empty-nest older adults aged 65 and above from the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS2018). Anxiety symptoms, depressive symptoms, and QoL were respectively assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale-7 (GAD-7), the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale-10 (CESD-10), and the World Health Organization Quality of Life-brief (WHOQOL-Bref). Co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms were defined as concurrent CESD-10 ≥ 10 and GAD-7 ≥ 5. We performed network analyses of co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms to identify central and bridge symptoms, and constructed a flow network to examine their associations with QoL. Multivariable linear regression analyses were conducted to assess the associations between symptom-status groups and QoL after adjustment for potential confounders.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The prevalence of co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms among Chinese empty-nest older adults was 8.67%. Network analysis revealed CESD3 (felt depressed), GAD4 (trouble relaxing) and GAD2 (uncontrollable worry) exhibited relatively high expected influence (EI) values within the anxiety and depressive symptom network. Concurrently, GAD1 (nervousness), GAD4 (trouble relaxing), CESD1 (bothered by things), and CESD6 (felt fearful) were identified as potential bridge symptoms between anxiety and depressive symptom communities. Moreover, CESD10 (sleep disturbances) showed a relatively strong negative association with quality of life (QoL). After adjustment for potential confounders, all three symptom groups had significantly lower QoL scores than the control group (depression-only: β = -0.96; anxiety-only: β = -0.33; co-occurring symptoms: β = -1.28; all p ≤ 0.001). Pairwise comparisons further showed that the co-occurring symptoms group had lower QoL scores than both the depression-only group (mean difference = -0.32, p < 0.001) and the anxiety-only group (mean difference = -0.95, p < 0.001).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Co-occurring anxiety and depressive symptoms are relatively common among Chinese empty-nest older adults and are significantly associated with poorer quality of life. It is important to pay attention to both central and bridge symptoms when assessing mental health in this population. Interventions aimed at addressing sleep disturbances among empty-nest older adults may be beneficial for supporting their mental health and improving their quality of life.

items.title: Clinical and Psychosocial Correlates of Cigarette Smoking in Psychiatric Inpatients.
items.authors: Sarubbi S, Migliorati M, Rogante E, Berardelli I, Comparelli A, Erbuto D, Innamorati M, Pompili M.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Tobacco smoking is an important issue due to its high prevalence in the general population and for its health consequences. Smoking is also frequently associated with mental disorders, with more severe clinical conditions and negative psychosocial outcomes.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: The present study investigated the sociodemographic and clinical correlates of cigarette smoking among psychiatric inpatients.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: Cross-sectional, observational study.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The sample included 408 inpatients, assessed for sociodemographic variables, psychiatric diagnoses, age at illness onset, previous psychiatric hospitalizations, and risk of suicide and non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI). Participants were divided into 2 groups: smokers and non-smokers, and groups were compared for the variables investigated. Then, the variables associated with smoking status were entered into a logistic regression model.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: About 65% of participants were smokers. Smoking patients had an earlier onset of the disorder, a higher frequency of previous hospitalizations, and were more frequently single and unemployed. In addition, smokers showed higher rates of alcohol use disorder (AUD), suicidal ideation, and NSSI. In the logistic regression model (Nagelkerke R ^2 = .183), previous psychiatric hospitalizations (OR = 1.96, P  = .007), being single (OR = 2.08, P  = .011), unemployment (OR = 1.68, P  = .028), current AUD (OR = 2.59, P  = .002), and current suicidal ideation (OR = 1.89, P  = .010) were independently associated with smoking status, while a later age at illness onset was inversely associated with tobacco use (OR = 0.98, P  = .024).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Our results show a strong association between cigarette smoking and indicators of clinical and psychosocial vulnerability in psychiatric inpatients, highlighting the need for systematic assessment of smoking habits and tailored interventions, including smoking cessation strategies.

items.title: Social, Educational, and Psychosocial Correlates of Lifetime Tobacco/Nicotine Initiation Status Among Adolescents in the 2019-2023 Korean Youth Health Behaviour Panel Survey.
items.authors: Le Tu H, Oh JK.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: This study examined the prevalence and correlates of lifetime tobacco/nicotine initiation status, defined as having ever initiated or used at least one tobacco/nicotine product among adolescents in South Korea.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We analyzed 22,843 adolescent-year observations from the 2019-2023 Korean Youth Health Behaviour Panel Survey. Survey-weighted prevalence estimates and sequential survey-weighted logistic regression models were used to examine associations of lifetime initiation status with socioeconomic indicators, academic performance, peer and household smoking, peer pressure, depressive feelings, access-related factors, and media/commercial exposure.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Overall, 647 adolescent-year observations (2.8%) were classified as having lifetime tobacco/nicotine initiation status. Weighted prevalence was 0.35% in 2019 and 9.07% in 2023, although the 2023 estimate should be interpreted cautiously because of outcome construction and missingness. In the fully adjusted model, lifetime initiation status was strongly associated with having one, two, or three close friends who smoked (AOR = 6.13, 11.07, and 22.31, respectively). Lower academic performance, depressive feelings, peer pressure to smoke, and male sex were also positively associated. Household economic status showed a non-monotonic pattern in the primary categorical analysis, while pocket money adequacy, access-related factors, and media/commercial exposure showed weaker or less consistent associations after full adjustment.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings highlight peer social context, educational vulnerability, and adolescent mental health as potentially relevant considerations for prevention.

items.authors: Maynard BR, Blumhagen HM, Matthieu MM, Maynard JA, Hyde R.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Suicide prevention among military personnel and veterans is a public health priority, yet evidence regarding effective interventions is dispersed across systematic reviews of varying scope and quality.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: To systematically identify, appraise, and synthesize reviews of suicide prevention and treatment interventions for military personnel and veterans and assess the applicability and quality of the evidence.

items.title: Acute Psychosis and Suicide Attempt As Manifestations of Severe Endogenous Hypercortisolism: A Case Report of Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH)-Independent Cushing Syndrome.
items.authors: Ortiz E, Martel N, Rojas C, Acosta Crousset Y, Ibanez Vasquez D.

sections.text: Cushing syndrome is an endocrine disorder caused by chronic exposure to excess cortisol. Although neuropsychiatric manifestations are common, progression to acute psychosis with a suicide attempt is exceptionally rare. We present the case of a patient with adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-independent Cushing syndrome secondary to a cortisol-secreting adrenocortical carcinoma, whose predominant neuropsychiatric manifestation was an acute psychotic episode with a suicide attempt. The patient had a five-month history of Cushingoid signs and symptoms, followed by one week of emotional lability that rapidly progressed to an acute psychotic episode with a suicide attempt prior to surgical resection, requiring hospitalization and psychiatric evaluation. Open adrenalectomy was performed, and histopathological examination confirmed a cortisol-secreting adrenocortical carcinoma. Subsequently, the patient experienced rapid resolution of psychiatric symptoms and a favorable clinical course following tumor resection. This case highlights the importance of considering hypercortisolism as a potentially reversible cause of acute psychosis and suicidal behavior. It also underscores the need to include endocrine disorders in the differential diagnosis of de novo psychosis and to incorporate early psychiatric evaluation into the multidisciplinary management of patients with Cushing syndrome, particularly in the presence of severe neuropsychiatric manifestations.

items.title: Acid-sensing ion channels in pain and psychiatric disorders: from basic properties to comorbidity mechanisms.
items.authors: Li C, Ye L, Qin S, Zeng Y, Sun Y, Lv H, Zhu C, Lin Y, Wan C.

sections.text: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are proton-gated cation channels that mediate Na^+ and Ca^2+ influx upon activation by extracellular acidification. Beyond protons, endogenous ligands, toxins, and small molecules modulate ASIC gating through direct or synergistic mechanisms. ASICs have emerged as key players in pain and psychiatric disorders. Tissue acidosis drives hyperalgesia via sustained ASIC activation, synaptic plasticity disruption, and central sensitization, thereby promoting chronic pain. In limbic circuits, ASIC1a expression in the amygdala, periaqueductal gray, and dorsal raphe nucleus links these channels to anxiety and depression, with ASIC1a antagonists demonstrating robust efficacy in preclinical models. Selective ASIC modulators represent promising therapeutic candidates for pain-psychiatric comorbidities. This review integrates ASIC biophysical properties with their molecular and circuit-level mechanisms in disease, offering a framework to guide future translational efforts targeting ASIC-mediated pathologies.

items.title: Involving palliative care: Development of a framework for people with life-threatening severe and enduring anorexia nervosa.
items.authors: Fauchère N, Zumbühl A, Krones T, Westermair AL, Feuz M, Pasi P, Hertler C, Blum D.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Anorexia nervosa is a severe metabo-psychosomatic disorder with high morbidity and mortality, predominantly affecting young women. Approximately 20% of anorectic patients develop a severe and enduring course (SE-AN), characterized by repeated unsuccessful specialized treatments, persistent underweight, and marked quality-of-life impairment. While current guidelines emphasize early, multimodal interventions with curative intent, therapeutic options become limited in treatment-refractory cases. Early palliative care integration has been proposed for chronic psychiatric disorders, including SE-AN. Given scarce structured frameworks for such integration, we aimed at developing a treatment framework based on a thorough clinical-ethical analysis and current evidence, integrating palliative care as an additional pathway for SE-AN patients in a University Hospital setting.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The standard operating procedure for anorexia nervosa at our tertiary referral centre was comprehensively revised in 2025. Based on structured literature review, clinical experience, and iterative consensus meetings, specialists from psychiatry, palliative care, and clinical ethics collaboratively developed a treatment framework for SE-AN. Ethical roundtables including palliative care specialists were established as core decision-making element.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Key ethical and clinical controversies were identified, regarding repeated coercive treatments, assessment of patients' decision-making capacity in severe malnutrition, and concerns about therapeutic futility versus abandonment. Complementing the existing curative pathway, two reversible, patient-centred palliative pathways were defined: (A) harm-reduction prioritizing quality-of-life while tolerating non-life-threatening underweight (BMI >14 kg/m^2), integrating somatic stabilization and specialized palliative support; and (B) a best supportive care/end-of-life approach for cases with predominant suffering and very low likelihood of quality-of-life improvement. Advance care planning was incorporated as essential component to ensure goal-concordant care, including emergency planning.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Structured integration of palliative care into SE-AN management provides an ethically grounded, interdisciplinary framework broadening therapeutic goals beyond weight normalization toward harm reduction and best-possible quality-of-life. Early, needs-based palliative involvement may reduce futile or burdensome interventions while maintaining openness to recovery-oriented care.

items.title: 'Not letting them set the music': a qualitative exploration of coping strategies for suicidal thoughts in an online support community.
items.authors: Marchionatti LE, Wagner L, De Souza Abdon APC, Barcellos C, Virtuoso E, Da Rosa KE, Amaral RR, Foletto MD, da Silva Magalhães PV.

sections.text: Interventions for suicidal ideation often focus on mitigating behaviours rather than addressing underlying cognitive processes. This study aims to explore coping mechanisms described by individuals reporting lived experiences with suicidal thoughts. We collected spontaneous narratives from non-identified users on a Reddit support community (r/depression). Data were extracted with an automated Python script scrapping threads related to suicidal ideation. We identified posts reporting first-hand experiences on coping and managing suicidal thoughts, which were explored with codebook thematic analysis. Analysis revealed a spectrum of attitudes towards suicidal thoughts, ranging from resistance to acceptance. Suicidal thoughts are a distressing experience leading to significant worry, and overemphasizing possible meanings or actively suppressing thoughts paradoxically increases their strength. Coping strategies included distraction, seeking social support and reframing thoughts. In particular, understanding and accepting thoughts may downsize their relevance. Validation emerged as a crucial factor in empowering individuals to regain control over their experiences. People struggling with suicidal thoughts may benefit from acceptance-oriented strategies and validation support. Engaging with suicidal ideation not solely as a risk but as a lived experience can open new avenues for research and care.

items.title: Psychometric Properties of the 3-Item Clinician Administered Dissociative States Scale (CADSS).
items.authors: Bremner JD, Vaccarino V.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: The 23-item Clinician Administered Dissociative States Scale (CADSS) has been widely used as a repeated measure of dissociative symptoms. A shortened version of the CADSS would be useful as a time-saving measure, especially for neurobiological studies of dissociation at multiple time points before and after an intervention. The purpose of this study was to assess the psychometric properties of two versions of a short form of the CADSS in a sample with and without posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Participants with (N=200) and without (N=315) the diagnosis of PTSD were assessed with the 23-item CADSS and/or the 3-item CADSS, the 6-item CADSS, and other psychometric and neuropsychological assessments. Analyses were performed to examine internal consistency, validity as measured by correlation with measures of PTSD and trauma, and sensitivity to change following exposure to personalized scripts of traumatic memories.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Both the 3-item CADSS (Cronbach's alpha 0.82) and the 6-item CADSS (Cronbach's alpha 0.81) showed good internal consistency. Validity for all versions was demonstrated based on correlations with other psychiatric symptom measures and ability to differentiate PTSD and non-PTSD participants. The 3-item CADSS demonstrated sensitivity to change based on a significant increase in scores after exposure to personalized traumatic scripts.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Both short form versions of the CADSS have acceptable psychometric properties.

items.title: Cocaine-Induced Severe Rhabdomyolysis with Acute Kidney Injury: A Case Report of Massively Elevated Creatine Kinase Exceeding 1,000,000 U/L.
items.authors: Belbase S, Khan U, Usman A, Elobeid O, Marcus H.

sections.text: Cocaine-associated rhabdomyolysis is a serious complication of stimulant intoxication characterized by skeletal muscle injury with the release of intracellular contents into the circulation, potentially resulting in acute kidney injury (AKI), severe electrolyte abnormalities, and other life-threatening complications. Fentanyl was also detected, but its contribution is difficult to determine. A 33-year-old male with a history of polysubstance use disorder presented after being found unresponsive on the floor with a posterior scalp laceration. He was combative during transport and arrived confused and obtunded. Urine drug screening was positive for cocaine and fentanyl (presumptive, unconfirmed); serum ethanol was 19 mg/dL. Initial laboratory evaluation demonstrated severe rhabdomyolysis with creatine kinase (CK) of 67,705 U/L, rising to a peak of 1,233,505 U/L on hospital day 2; pigmenturia suggestive of myoglobinuria; hyperkalemia (8.3 mEq/L); hypocalcemia (5.6 mg/dL); hyperphosphatemia (9 mg/dL); high anion gap metabolic acidosis (anion gap 21 mEq/L, lactate 18.8 mmol/L); and stage 3 AKI, with creatinine of 1.3 mg/dL on arrival, peaking at 5.7 mg/dL on hospital day 11. Electrocardiography demonstrated peaked T-wave morphology consistent with hyperkalemia. Emergency management included intravenous calcium gluconate, insulin-dextrose therapy, sodium bicarbonate, fluid resuscitation, and emergent hemodialysis. Hemoadsorption therapy for myoglobin removal was considered but was unavailable. After improvement in mental status, left foot drop was recognized on hospital day 4. Evaluation revealed acute compartment syndrome (ACS) of the left lower extremity, requiring emergent anterior and lateral fasciotomy followed by multiple wound washouts, serial debridement, and wound vacuum-assisted closure exchanges. The patient was ultimately discharged on outpatient hemodialysis three times weekly, with wound care, surgical follow-up, and referral for substance use disorder counseling and harm reduction services. Renal recovery was documented about 12 weeks after presentation. This case highlights an extreme presentation of cocaine-associated rhabdomyolysis complicated by profound rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI, life-threatening metabolic derangements, and delayed recognition of ACS. Early recognition, fluid resuscitation, timely renal replacement therapy, and continued neurological surveillance beyond the acute metabolic phase are critical for optimizing outcomes. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for compartment syndrome and should not rely on classic signs in patients with severe rhabdomyolysis.

items.title: Partitioned feature selection: locally uniform feature selection with structured feature grouping for explainable predictor identification.
items.authors: Shaha TR, Al Farid F, Begum M, Al Mamun A, Nazneen T, Uddin J, Abdul Karim HB.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Feature selection helps identify important features in high-dimensional mental health data. However, conventional feature selection (CFS) methods commonly rank all features within a single feature space using an overall statistical or predictive criterion. This global evaluation method does not take into account the fact that symptoms of depression are interrelated and fall within various distinct clinical domains. To address this limitation, we propose partitioned feature selection (PFS), a framework that integrates domain-based feature grouping with group-wise feature selection.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: PFS organizes depression symptoms into clinically relevant domains and applies four complementary feature selection methods to estimate individual feature importance within each domain. The importance scores are normalized and combined, then weighted according to each domain's association with global severity to calculate integrated group feature importance (IGFI). We evaluated PFS on two independent multiclass depression datasets using 16 classifiers. Validation-guided feature retention was used to select the final feature subsets. We also conducted a ten-trial random regrouping analysis, an exploratory Wilcoxon signed-rank comparison with CFS-RFE, and a comparison of IGFI rankings with SHAP explanations.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: PFS selected 21 features for Dataset 1 and 23 features for Dataset 2. Using the selected, untuned support vector classifier (SVC) configuration without synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE), PFS achieved test accuracies of 95.65% and 89.60% and Macro-F1 scores of 95.43% and 92.37%, respectively. The random regrouping analysis showed that the predictive effect of clinical partitioning varied between datasets. The exploratory Wilcoxon analysis also showed dataset-dependent statistical differences between PFS and CFS-RFE. Furthermore, IGFI and SHAP identified similar important features across clinical domains.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: PFS provides a structured approach to identifying important depression symptoms while preserving their clinical domain information. The findings indicate that domain-based grouping can support interpretability, although its predictive benefits vary across datasets. This study focuses on questionnaire-based depression severity estimation rather than the prediction of an independently established clinical diagnosis.

items.title: Impulse control symptoms associated with aripiprazole long-acting injectable: A prospective cohort study.
items.authors: López García FJ, de Marco Galliano G, López Soto MD, Vallès Callol V, Penadés Rubio R, Aragay Vicente N.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Impulse control disorders (ICDs) have been described in association with dopamine partial agonists, particularly aripiprazole. However, data regarding the risk of ICDs with long-acting injectable (LAI) formulations remain limited.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: To prospectively examine the presence and course of impulse control symptoms in psychiatric patients treated with intramuscular aripiprazole, compared with paliperidone and risperidone, over six months of follow-up.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: Prospective cohort study.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a prospective cohort study in a naturalistic clinical setting to evaluate the emergence of impulse control symptoms in patients treated with aripiprazole LAI. 27 patients initiating intramuscular treatment with aripiprazole (n=17), paliperidone (n=6), or risperidone (n=4) were systematically assessed monthly for pathological gambling, compulsive buying, hypersexuality, alcohol use, and other substance use. Repeated-measures ANOVA and linear mixed-effects models were applied.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Clinically significant impulse control symptoms emerged in a proportion of patients treated with aripiprazole LAI, particularly compulsive buying. Symptom presentation was heterogeneous. While most monitored behaviours followed comparable longitudinal trajectories across treatment groups, compulsive buying showed a significant group-by-time interaction, characterized by a peak at month 3 among patients receiving aripiprazole.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: These findings suggest that aripiprazole LAI may be associated with the emergence of impulse control symptoms in a subset of patients. Although preliminary, this study highlights the importance of systematic monitoring of behavioral side effects in patients receiving LAI formulations of dopamine partial agonists. Further research with larger samples is warranted to better characterize this association.

items.title: Has the gap increased? A longitudinal cohort study of social inequalities in mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic from the HUNT Study, Norway.
items.authors: Weiss D, Lowenstein C, Sund ER, Vethe D, Krokstad S.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Evidence on the long-term mental health consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic remains mixed, particularly considering existing social inequalities. Longitudinal population-based studies are needed to assess late-stage and postpandemic mental health trajectories and gradients.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a cohort study using data from the Norwegian Trøndelag Health Study (HUNT). Adult participants (n=32 743) who completed both the prepandemic HUNT4 survey (2017-2019) and the HUNT-COVID survey (2021-2023) were included. Outcomes included general psychological distress (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, total score), loneliness and self-reported health (SRH). items.title: Quantitative evaluation of student mental health policies in China: an LDA-PMC coupled approach.
items.authors: Li W, Wang X, Liu X, Zhao B, Zhang H.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Quantitative evaluation of student mental health policies remains methodologically underdeveloped, with most existing studies relying on qualitative assessments or manually constructed indicators that introduce subjective bias.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Drawing on Self-Determination Theory and the Biopsychosocial Technological Systems Theory, this study develops a data-driven evaluation framework by integrating TF-IDF keyword extraction, Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling, and the Policy Modeling Consistency (PMC) index model. A three-tier scoring system is applied to 22 national and provincial student mental health policy documents issued in China between 2001 and 2025; secondary indicators were scored on a three-tier scale (0, 0.5, or 1), primary indicators were calculated as their means, and the PMC score was computed as the sum of the ten primary indicators.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The LDA analysis identifies five latent policy topics: curriculum and faculty development, risk prevention and intervention, home-school-community collaboration, resource assurance, and evaluation and innovation; a seed-locked re-estimation with adjacent K = 4 and K = 6 solutions confirmed the robustness of this five-topic solution. These topics directly inform the construction of 10 primary and 44 secondary PMC indicators. The results indicate that overall policy quality is moderate (mean PMC score = 6.56, range: 3.17 to 8.23), with 59.1% of policies rated as excellent (PMC: 7.00 to 8.99), 18.2% as good (PMC: 5.00 to 6.99), and 22.7% as weak (PMC: 0.00 to 4.99). Policies perform well on transparency (indicator score 0.85), domain coverage (0.84), and policy nature (0.83), but exhibit consistent structural weaknesses in legal enforceability (0.36), multi-departmental coordination (0.35), and medium- to long-term planning (0.42). Heterogeneity analysis reveals three patterns: policy documents have become increasingly comprehensive and standardized from the exploratory phase (2001 to 2010) through the deepening phase (2021 to 2025); contrary to H2, provincial-level documents on average scored higher than national-level ones, a pattern largely attributable to the composition of the sample; and eastern and western regions scored similarly high, with central-region documents lower.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: These findings suggest that while China's student mental health policy framework has matured in scope and standardization, it remains constrained by low legislative hierarchy, fragmented governance, and insufficient institutional support for family-school-community coordination.

items.title: Research on the integration model of children's mental health education and innovative thinking from the perspective of positive psychology.
items.authors: Ge J, Gu W.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: At present, children's mental health empowerment and innovative thinking cultivation are insufficient, and an integrated education system has not yet been formed. Based on the theoretical framework of positive psychology, this study constructs an integrated model of children's mental health education and innovative thinking cultivation.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A retrospective control design was adopted in this study. The data of children's follow-up education were collected, and 320 valid samples were screened. According to different psychological intervention methods, they were divided into observation group and control group with 160 cases in each group. The control group adopted the conventional mental health education mode, while the observation group implemented the positive psychology-oriented integrated cultivation mode of mental health and innovative thinking. With Psychological Wellbeing (PWB), Connor-Davidson Children's Psychological Resilience Scale (CD-RISC) and Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking (TTCT) as the core indicators. Observable confounding bias is controlled by propensity score matching (PSM), path correlation between variables is tested by maximum likelihood estimation of structural equation model (SEM), and the single-intermediary effect is tested by deviation correction. The combined reliability (CR) and the average variance extraction were used.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: After the intervention, the scores of psychological wellbeing, psychological resilience and innovative thinking in the observation group were significantly higher than those in the control group. After propensity score matching (PSM) matching, the baseline equilibrium between the two groups was comparable, and the model CR > 0.82 and average variance extraction (AVE)>0.51, with good aggregation validity; The structural equation model shows that the total effect of integration mode on children's innovative thinking is 0.610, and positive psychological quality plays a partial mediating role, and the mediating effect accounts for 43.78% of the total effect. The test-retest reliability of the intra-class correlation coefficient (ICC) of each dimension is 0.924, and the data reliability is excellent.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The integrated mode of positive psychological guidance is related to the improvement of children's positive psychological literacy and innovative thinking level, which suggests the intermediary transmission mechanism of multi-dimensional positive psychological factors and provides practical reference for the integrated cultivation of children's psychological education and innovative literacy.

items.title: Artificial intelligence applications in fMRI-based disease diagnosis: A systematic review.
items.authors: Almetwally EM, Diab LS, Ahmed MA, Kamel AR.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: The purpose of this study is to critically assess and thoroughly explore the use of artificial intelligence (AI) methods in functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) for the diagnosis of neuropsychiatric and neurological conditions. Methodological variability, dataset features, validation techniques, repeatability transparency, and the clinical preparedness of AI-based diagnostic models are the main topics of the review.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A thorough search for research published between 2010 and 2025 was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore. The review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. The PICOS framework was used to define the eligibility requirements. Studies were included if they published quantitative performance metrics and used resting-state or task-based fMRI data in conjunction with machine learning or deep learning models for disease classification. A modified QUADAS-2 framework appropriate for AI-based diagnostic research was used to evaluate the methodological quality and bias risk. Because study designs, datasets, preprocessing pipelines, and evaluation metrics varied, the data were synthesized qualitatively.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: After the PRISMA 2020 screening procedure, 80 studies in all satisfied the inclusion requirements. The majority of research concentrated on autistic spectrum disorder, Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, and major depressive disorder. While machine learning methods (especially support vector machines) and deep learning architectures like convolutional neural networks and graph neural networks were the most commonly used artificial intelligence techniques, resting-state fMRI was the most commonly used imaging modality. In general, reported categorization accuracy fell between 85% and 96%. Nonetheless, significant methodological variation was noted in model topologies, validation techniques, feature extraction techniques, and preprocessing pipelines. Concerns about the generalizability of the model and possible overfitting were highlighted by the frequent dependence on very small cohorts and the sparse use of external validation. Additionally, quality assessment revealed moderate to high risks of bias in several studies, especially in relation to validation and patient selection processes.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The use of AI to analyze fMRI data shows great promise for enhancing the diagnostic categorization of neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders. However, clinical translation is restricted by small sample sizes, inconsistent methods, and a lack of external validation. To improve repeatability and facilitate the incorporation of AI-driven fMRI analysis into clinical practice, standardized preprocessing procedures, bigger multi-site datasets, open reporting procedures, and stringent external validation are necessary.

items.title: Fear memory expression and reconsolidation depend on hippocampal astrocytic glutamate uptake in male rats.
items.authors: Renfijes MM, Riboldi JG, Iribarne J, Medina JH, Viola H.

sections.text: The control of glutamate levels in the synaptic gap is crucial for neuronal communication, as it prevents excitotoxicity from excessive receptor activation. Glutamate transporters GLT-1 are mainly localized in astrocytes and its expression is particularly abundant in the hippocampus (Hp). In this study, we explored the role of GLT-1 in consolidation, expression and reconsolidation of memory, using contextual fear conditioning (CFC) task. Dihydrokainic acid (DHK), a selective GLT-1 inhibitor, was injected into the dorsal Hp of male rats at different times around aversive learning. DHK administration 15 min after a weak CFC training session promoted long-term memory (LTM) formation. However, DHK administration around strong CFC training sessions did not affect memory consolidation. Moreover, DHK infusion 15 min before the LTM test session impaired CFC memory expression. Importantly, if applied 15 min after a reactivation session, DHK impairs CFC reconsolidation. In contrast, the antibiotic ceftriaxone (CFT), which increases GLT-1 expression, did not affect the consolidation or the expression of fear memory. The effects of DHK and CFT on memory were not due to changes in locomotor activity or anxiety-like state of rats. In conclusion, our findings indicate that inhibition of hippocampal astroglial glutamate uptake impairs the expression and reconsolidation of aversive memory without impairing its consolidation, and highlight potential therapeutic avenues for neuropsychiatric conditions, including phobias, post-traumatic stress disorder, and cognitive deficits.

items.title: Effectiveness of mobile applications in pregnancy care: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
items.authors: Mehrabi R, Bagherzadeh Z, Akbari S, Askari F.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Mobile health applications are increasingly integrated into antenatal care as supportive tools to enhance maternal knowledge, promote healthy behaviors, and improve clinical and psychosocial outcomes.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This umbrella review aimed to synthesize and critically appraise evidence on the effectiveness of mobile applications in pregnancy care.

sections.heading: Materials and methods
sections.text: A systematic search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, and Web of Science, without language restrictions. Search terms included "mobile applications" and "pregnancy". This umbrella review synthesized evidence from 21 systematic reviews and meta-analyses published up to May 17, 2025, covering 180 randomized controlled trials with sample sizes ranging from 456-10,348 participants. The methodological quality of eligible articles was assessed using AMSTAR 2.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Findings consistently showed that mobile applications can improve maternal knowledge, self-management, physical activity, diet, weight control, and adherence to prenatal care recommendations. Positive effects were also reported for mental health, including reductions in stress and depressive symptoms, while evidence suggested decreased cesarean section rates, neonatal intensive care admissions, and adverse maternal-fetal outcomes. Despite encouraging results, the overall evidence is constrained by methodological limitations, heterogeneous app designs, small sample sizes, short follow-up periods, and incomplete reporting, reducing the strength and generalizability of conclusions.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Mobile health interventions demonstrate considerable potential as complementary strategies in prenatal care. Future research should focus on high-quality, large-scale, long-term trials with culturally sensitive, personalized approaches. Strong collaboration among researchers, healthcare providers, and technology developers is essential to fully harness the impact of mobile applications on maternal and neonatal health.

items.title: Identifying characteristics and behavioral phenotypes of musculoskeletal disorders using wearables in All of Us.
items.authors: Yan AY, Speed TJ, Taylor CO.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Wearable devices provide continuous measures of daily activity, sleep, and heart-rate (HR)-derived characteristics, creating new opportunities for digital phenotyping of musculoskeletal disorders (MSD). However, longitudinal behavioral patterns and heterogeneity among individuals with MSD remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify characteristics associated with MSD and characterize behavioral phenotypes using longitudinal wearable data.

sections.heading: Materials and methods
sections.text: We analyzed 2344 participants (MSD = 1036; non-MSD = 1308) from the All of Us Research Program. First, supervised machine-learning models were trained using sociodemographic, physical measurement, and wearable-derived features to distinguish individuals with and without MSD and identify factors associated with MSD status. Model interpretation was performed using SHapley Additive exPlanations values. Second, temporal profiling and unsupervised clustering were applied to 90-day wearable trajectories of participants with MSD to identify behavioral phenotypes.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: XGBoost achieved the best classification performance (accuracy = 0.929, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.930, area under the precision-recall curve = 0.870, F1 = 0.919). Important factors associated with MSD included lower activity, longer sleep, and female sex. Behavioral phenotyping identified 5 distinct phenotypes differing in activity patterns, sleep characteristics, HR-derived measures, pain burden, mental health conditions, and employment status. Notably, high-pain phenotypes exhibited greater prevalence of anxiety and depressive disorders, lower pulse rate variability, and distinct sleep profiles compared with more active phenotypes. These phenotypes demonstrated moderate reproducibility in bootstrap-based stability analysis (mean adjusted rand index = 0.62).

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Longitudinal wearable data revealed behavioral heterogeneity among individuals with MSD that was not fully explained by traditional diagnostic categories. items.title: Multimorbidity in patients with chronic liver disease: A systematic review.
items.authors: Lozano-Chacon B, Ortega-Martín E, Pérez-Mejía J, Camacho-García M, Alvarez-Galvez J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Chronic liver disease (CLD) is a major global health threat traditionally managed through a "hepatocentric" lens, which often overlooks the systemic complexity of the disease. This systematic review aims to identify multimorbidity patterns (clusters) in adults with CLD and evaluate their specific impact on clinical outcomes and mortality risk.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A systematic search was performed across PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, and Web of Science for studies published until July 2025. Following PRISMA guidelines, 19 high-quality studies (12 cohort and 7 cross-sectional) were selected. We analysed multimorbidity clusters, focusing on cardiometabolic, mental health, and musculoskeletal domains, and extracted effect sizes (HR and OR) to determine prognostic impact.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Multimorbidity affects up to 99% of patients with CLD. Three primary clusters were identified: the cardiometabolic cluster, linked to the Liver-Cardio-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome; the mental health cluster, where depression increases mortality risk by 49% (HR 1.49); and the musculoskeletal cluster, where myosteatosis is associated with a 2.9-fold increased risk of severe fibrosis (OR 2.9). Notably, the presence of two or more extrahepatic conditions doubles the mortality risk (HR 2.00). These findings demonstrate that extrahepatic clusters are independent predictors of poor prognosis in patients with liver dysfunction.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The survival of CLD patients depends on the totality of the disease network rather than isolated hepatic function. Effective management requires a transition to an integrated multidisciplinary model, incorporating routine screening for sarcopenia and mental health disorders to mitigate systemic frailty.

items.title: Toward a Preliminary Conceptual Framework for Managing Aggressive Behaviour in Psychiatric Facilities: A Qualitative Study of Mental Health Practitioners' Perspectives.
items.authors: Rathobei LM, Mkhize SW.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Aggressive behaviour among people with severe mental illness (PSMI) can jeopardise the safety of patients, staff, and the therapeutic environment, posing serious challenges for mental health professionals (MHPs). Despite existing management strategies, an evidence-based implementation framework is needed to guide consistent management of aggressive behaviour in psychiatric facilities in Lesotho.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: An exploratory, descriptive qualitative design was used at a mental health facility in southern districts of Lesotho. Data were collected between February and June 2021 through semi-structured individual interviews with nine MHPs and one focus group discussion with six participants. Thematic analysis was used to identify key strategies to inform the implementation framework.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Five themes emerged: psychotherapeutic and de-escalation interventions; containment and environmental safety strategies; pharmacological management of aggression; workforce capacity and organisational enablement; and governance, policy, and regulatory structures. These themes informed development of a preliminary conceptual framework intended to guide, rather than prescribe, future implementation efforts.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: MHPs regard an evidence-based implementation strategy as essential to better managing aggressive behaviour. The resulting preliminary framework offers a conceptual foundation for future work on strengthening clinical practice, staff preparedness, patient safety, and the consistent application of evidence-based management techniques, pending further validation.

items.title: MomWay: A human-centered mHealth app prototype for postpartum wellness.
items.authors: Edayath P, Guevara Mendoza J, Sanchez-Balandran J, Pennathur A, Pennathur PR.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To describe the formative development of MomWay, a human-centered mobile health (mHealth) prototype designed to support postpartum mothers during the critical recovery period following childbirth.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We employed a user-experience design approach using the double diamond framework and product design guidelines. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with three postpartum mothers in a U.S.-Mexico border community in this exploratory, formative prototype-design study to explore postpartum experiences, barriers to care, and support needs. Interview data were synthesized through needs identification, affinity mapping to identify user need categories, followed by competitive benchmarking, and persona development. These insights informed iterative development of medium-fidelity prototypes.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Mothers described reliance on internet searches for postpartum information, frustration with overwhelming or contradictory guidance, and limitations in existing maternal health apps particularly related to mental health support and comprehensive recovery tracking. Six categories of user needs emerged: reliable information, educational resources, tracking and management, mental health support, personalization, and improved functionality compared to existing apps. The resulting MomWay prototype proposes design features for personalized onboarding, physical and mental health recovery tracking, curated educational resources, support groups, appointment management, AI-assisted question answering, and direct provider communication features.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Formative human-centered design methods enabled translation of postpartum mothers' needs into a digital health prototype addressing access-related, cultural, and informational barriers in postpartum care. MomWay demonstrates how early-stage user research can inform mHealth intervention development in culturally diverse communities. Future work will evaluate usability, feasibility and implementation.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and immersive technologies for LGBTQ+ youth: a narrative review.
items.authors: Shekarchi R, Eleuteri S, Saladino V, Calaresi D, Giordano F, Prunas A.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, and other sexual and gender minority (LGBTQ+) youth face elevated rates of mental health difficulty alongside persistent barriers to affirming professional care. AI-powered chatbots and virtual reality (VR) and metaverse environments have both been proposed as ways of reaching this population, but the two literatures have developed separately, and we identified no review covering both for LGBTQ+ youth specifically.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To map current applications of AI chatbots and VR/metaverse tools for LGBTQ+ youth, examine risks related to algorithmic bias and online safety, consider how digital environments may support identity affirmation, and identify priorities for research and practice.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a narrative review; a format suited to evidence that is sparse and varied in design. Searches ran across PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar using seven search string combinations, supplemented by reference list screening and citation tracking. Of 367 records from the original search and 180 from a supplementary search, 67 sources informed the synthesis; 12 provided direct evidence from LGBTQ+ young people. Empirical studies were appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Four themes emerged. AI chatbots are acceptable to LGBTQ+ young people and valued for their anonymity, but current tools give generic responses and perform poorly outside North American and Western European contexts. VR and metaverse environments support avatar-based identity exploration and embodied community connection, with early evidence of feasibility for transgender and gender expansive youth. Algorithmic bias is a documented harm, operating through content moderation, facial recognition, and language model outputs. In co-design studies, LGBTQ+ young people identified gaps that developers had missed, although no study has yet compared co-designed tools with conventionally developed ones.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: These technologies have real potential, but the evidence base does not yet support strong claims. Most studies are pilot or feasibility designs with small samples, concentrated in a handful of high-income countries. Progress requires more rigorous trials, greater geographic diversity, wider use of participatory design, tested against conventional development, and outcome measures that capture affirmation as well as symptom reduction, for which validated instruments do not yet exist.

items.title: Household work participation is associated with adolescent mental health through parent-child relationship and resilience.
items.authors: Yan C, Qu Y.

sections.text: Adolescent mental health is a central concern in educational psychology and youth development. This study used data from a school-based survey on 1,152 junior middle school students in Xi'an, China and examined whether and how participation in household work was associated with adolescent mental health. We assessed a serial mediation model in which parent-child relationship and adolescent resilience were specified as potential mediators. Results revealed that household work participation was positively correlated with adolescent mental health, parent-child relationship, and resilience. Furthermore, household work participation was significantly associated with greater perceived closeness with parents and higher resilience, after adjusting for gender, grade, only-child status, academic performance, hukou status, school type, family structure, and parental education. Bootstrap mediation analyses indicated that the association between household work participation and mental health was consistent with an indirect-effects pattern that involved parent-child relationship, resilience, and their serial pathway. Among the indirect pathways, the resilience pathway accounted for the largest proportion of the total indirect effect. These findings suggest that household work may represent a meaningful family-based context associated with adolescent psychological well-being, greater perceived closeness with parents, and stronger psychological resources. This study contributes to research on adolescent mental health by highlighting the educational and developmental value of household work within family life.
